newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses mixed, dlr/Swiss hits 4-yr high.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses mixed, dlr/Swiss hits 4-yr high.

text.p: European stocks were mixed on Monday, with markets trying to shrug off Wall Street's decline on Friday and focus on domestic factors to provide near-term direction.

The dollar climbed to a four-year high against the Swiss franc in early trade to catch up with recent gains in dollar/mark to near eight-year peaks, traders said. Swiss markets were closed on Friday for a holiday.
"The dollar...was breaking out (higher) at Friday's close and gave a pretty obvious signal to buty dollars and sell Swiss francs," said Adam Beaudin, market strategist at CSFB in Zurich.
The dollar climbed as high as 1.5326 Swiss francs in early trade, its first visit above 1.53 since August 1993 and up from Thursday's close near 1.5130, before the Swiss holiday.

Against the yen, the dollar was little changed from late Friday's levels despite the dollar's brief drop overnight in Tokyo after a Japanese official's remarks in an interview with Dow Jones news agency.
Economic Planning Agency's Taro Aso was quoted as saying in an interview on Sunday that an official Japanese discount rate rise was "very possible" by year end.
But the dollar recovered, with institutional investors still willing to buy dollars on dips because the overall U.S. economy continued to look strong.
The dollar's continued buoyancy helped underpin most European bourses, but equity traders were more concerned with corporate earnings and domestic interest rate trends.
London's FTSE-100 index erased losses after HSBC Holdings Plc soared to a year high of 2,326 pence on better-than-expected first-half results.

The bank said pre-tax profits in sterling terms rose 13 percent to 2.623 billion pounds ($4.3 billion), with dividends up 33 percent to 20 pence per share. That compares with analysts' forecasts for pre-tax profits between 2.32 and 2.48 billion pounds.
But FTSE activity was expected to be limited with interest rate worries looming. The Bank of England's monetary policy-setting meeting is on Wednesday and Thursday.
A Reuters poll taken on July 30 showed 16 of 23 economists expected official British interest rates to rise 25 basis points after the meeting for the fourth rate rise in so many months.
Germany's DAX index fell sharply in early trade, shedding more than two percent, led by losses in bank stocks.
Commerzbank AG was down 0.85 mark at 61.80, Deutsche Bank AG down 2.65 at 119.50, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG down 3.15 at 72.80 and Bay Vereinsbank was down 1.90 at 96.90.
But German losses are expected to remain capped by the dollar's steady rise against the mark. A weaker currency makes goods cheaper abroad, which is seen boosting exports.
French shares eased after a stronger opening amid thin holiday trade. But traders expected losses there to also be limited by the dollar's strength.
Finland's FOX index edged up, ignoring the Dow Jones Industrial Average's 28.57-point loss on Friday to 8,194.04, as traders awaited Nokia Ab Oy's second-quarter report at 1300 GMT.

The mobile phone maker was expected to post impressive earnings after Ericsson posted better-than-expected results more than a week ago. Analysts forecast Nokia's second-quarter pre-tax profits at 1.64 billion markka ($295.4 million), up from 728 million a year ago.
But one broker said: "I think it would have to be 1.7 to 1.8 billion to justify this (Nokia's share) price."
Nokia shares hit a year high of 485 markka in early trade, and the FOX index was up 3.67 points at 1,241.85 at midmorning.
Dutch stocks also rose in anticpation of second-quarter results from several blue-chip companies.

Steel and aluminum group Koninklijke Nederlandsche Hoogovens en Staalfabrieken NV shares jumped to a year high of 139.80 guilders ($66.59) on expectations of solid earnings growth when it reports on Wednesday.
"We're not negative on those figures and neither is the market," a dealer said, adding that the shares should also benefit because it is a cyclical stock.
CURRENCIES AT 0950 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8697 marks and 118.50 yen compared to 1.8630 and 118.37 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0950 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 4.3 points at 4,903.60.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 84.95 points in bourse trade at 4,323.84.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 17.76 points at 3,031.68.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at 1030 in London at $324.05, down from Friday's close at $324.25. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
($ = 5.552 Finnish Markka)
($ = 2.099 Dutch Guilders)
